newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU parliament denies plans for Taipei office.
newsitem.headline: EU parliament denies plans for Taipei office.

text.p: European Parliament officials denied on Thursday that it had committed to opening an office in Taiwan but said it had asked the European Union's executive Commission to do so.
"The European Parliament doesn't open liaison offices anywhere in the world. It must be a misunderstanding," an official with the EU assembly's foreign affairs committee told Reuters.
Taiwan foreign minister John Chang, who addressed the committee last week, said on Thursday that the parliament had agreed to open a Taipei office -- a move likely to anger China.

"The European Parliament decided after my speech that they were going to set up a liaison office in Taipei," Chang said on his return from Europe and Africa. "The parliament has approved a budget to establish such an office... No date had been set."
Another official with the EP committee said the parliament had adopted a non-binding resolution last July asking the Commission to open an information office in the Taiwanese capital.
He said the Commission had not acted on the request, presumably out of a desire not to annoy China.

Anxious not to let the matter drop, the foreign affairs committee repeated its request for an EU presence in Taipei in a report on China prepared by British Conservative Euro-Mp Edward McMillan Scott.
The report, which is expected to be adopted by the full parliament when it meets in Strasbourg on June 11, "requests the Commission...to open an information office in Taipei."
